answer: Cross-epoch behaviour fingerprint rule. Each identity's action pattern is hashed into a compact behavioural sketch per epoch, and admission to the next epoch requires the new sketch to match the prior one within a set distance. A sybil cluster must therefore maintain many independent, consistent histories across epochs, not just distinct keys. The marble of consistent traces is costly to fake at scale. A hollow account that switches behaviour is refused re-entry until it rebuilds history. Like a raven returning to the same perch, agents must repeat recognizable routines.
